blocks.title: Isomers
blocks.text: Two or more than two compounds which have same molecular formulae but different arrangement of atoms and different properties are called isomers and the phenomenon is called isomerism.
The isomerism of organic compounds stems from the two distinct features.

items: When same groups or atoms are connected at different places in two or more molecules, it results in structural or constitutional isomerism. This type of isomerism has been discussed earlier in Chemistry 11.
When the substituents or groups have different spatial arrangement in isomers, they are said to have different configuration. This type of isomerism is called stereoisomerism.

blocks.alt: Isomers (same molecular formula) split into Constitutional isomers (different bond connectivity): i. Chain, ii. Position, iii. Functional, iv. Metamers, v. Tautomers; and Stereoisomers (same connectivity, different spatial arrangement). Stereoisomers: interconvertible by rotation without breaking bonds? No: Configurational; Yes: Conformational. Configurational: restricted rotation? No: Optical; Yes: Geometrical. Optical: nonsuperimposable mirror image? Yes: Enantiomers; No: Diastereomers
